key_insight: In laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, laser power, travel speed, and welding current jointly govern molten-pool flow, weld geometry, and arc stability.
engineering_relevance: These trends can guide parameter selection for welding low-expansion Invar tooling used to manufacture aerospace composites.
method: High-speed photography of pool evolution and arc behavior
Comparison across laser power, welding speed, and current ranges
evidence_signal: Across 5–6 kW, 0.5–0.8 m/min, and 150–170 A, higher power increased penetration and keyhole size, higher speed reduced penetration and width, and higher current widened the weld and stabilized the arc.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative validation errors or weld-quality metrics, so these parameter trends should not be treated as a qualified production window.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
